## 1 — ITEM 1: `H2` SURVIVES, AND I CAN SAY WHY

I could not find an input where `H2` is wrong. Five new hand inputs were written
specifically to break it and did not (`.temp/t137/logs/readpath.log`, section A):

```
       input |         R1 (bug)   H2 write-1site   H1 write-@free
  free+reins |       ASan-abort               OK               OK   free the saved leaf, then
                                                                    re-INSERT the same key --
                                                                    malloc hands back the address
 recyc+reins |   69224958356130               OK   69224958356130   recycle the saved node, then
                                                                    put its found key back in the tree
 recyc twice |   25211279021280               OK   25211279021280   TWO substitutions at the same record
 succ then v |       ASan-abort               OK               OK   delete the SUCCESSOR first
   find-miss |               OK               OK               OK   a FAILED find after a good one
```

plus **600 fresh windows: `H2 != model : 0 / 600`**, against `H1`'s `14 / 600`.
That is on top of the engineer's `0/1500` and `0/1200`.

> ### ✅ AND IT IS NOT LUCK. `H2` IS EXACT FOR A REASON, AND THE REASON IS WORTH PUTTING IN `spec.md`:
>
> Only two events can break *"the saved record still holds the key it was found
> under"*: the record is **freed**, or its key/val are **overwritten by its
> in-order successor's**. The iterative delete's cursor visits exactly those two
> records — the victim on the first turn, the successor on the second — so one
> site at the top of the loop covers both, and the successor is a minimum so it
> never re-enters the two-child branch.
> **And the saved record can never RE-ACQUIRE its found key**, because each
> substitution replaces a key with its in-order successor's, which is strictly
> greater: a fixed record's key is monotonically increasing. So *"null on first
> touch"* is not conservative-and-lucky, it is **exact**.
> **A false positive is impossible for a symmetric reason**: `tab[cur] == g_saved`
> could match a different record only after `g_saved`'s record was freed, which
> requires the site to have already fired, and `tab[cur]` is never `NULL` for a
> live cursor.

⚠⚠ **But the H2-vs-H3 comparison answered a question that is not the real one.**
The report reaches *"the safety line is on the WRITE path"* through §1d, and §1d
is false in the shape §2e pins. See §2.

### 2c — what actually distinguishes the two temporal rows, stated so it can be shipped

**`p27`'s read-path line is ONE conjunct — `live[h] == 1` — and `p29`'s is TWO:**
`live[g_slot] == 1 && tab[g_slot][0] == g_key`. The first conjunct is
**liveness of the ALLOCATION**; the second is **identity of the OCCUPANT**, and
it exists only because `p29`'s second bug class never touches the allocation.
⚠ **One conjunct is not enough and the failure is measurable, not arguable**:
drop the liveness half and you have `H4`, which is a `heap-use-after-free` on
41 of 400 windows; drop the key half and the recycle class goes undetected.

✅ **That is a stronger admissibility argument than the one in the report, and it
is the reviewed bar's limb 1 — *a new operator on the safety line* — as a
measurement rather than a story.** ⚠ It is also **less** differentiating than
*"the two rows are not the same shape"*: `p29`'s line is `p27`'s line **plus one
term**, on the same path, over the same state.

### 2d — ⚠ a consequence for the kernel shape, from `p27`'s own file

`patterns/p27-handle-table/c/kernel.c`'s header argues, at length and by name:

> *"Why the liveness bit cannot be 'the pointer is NULL'. … nulling `tab[h]` on
> close would turn the stale read into a NULL dereference, which is a **crash**,
> not a use-after-free, and a different bug class."*

⚠ **`TASK_136`'s pinned `p29` kernel does exactly that** — `free(tab[cur]);
live[cur] = 0; tab[cur] = NULL;`. It survives only because `p29`'s UAF runs
through `g_saved` rather than through `tab[]`. **Consequence: `T4` (via `tab[]`)
depends on a deviation from `p27`'s reasoned convention and `T3` (via `live[]`)
does not.** A `p29` that follows `p27` must use the `live[]` spelling. **Decide
this deliberately; do not inherit it.**

### 3b — ⚠⚠⚠ THE VERUS ROW. Not vacuous; and not what it is said to prove.

**Four clean negatives first, because they are the engineer's:**

| probe | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| `assert(false)` at the END of `arm_c` | must fail | **`5 verified, 1 errors`** — the path is reachable |
| `assert(false)` right after `rec_open` | must fail | **`5 verified, 1 errors`** — the `external_body` axioms are **not** contradictory, so nothing downstream is vacuous |
| `ensures r == 8` on a body that writes `9` | must fail | **`postcondition not satisfied`** — the postcondition reads the body |
| ARM_C rewritten through `p27`'s permission `Map`, the way ARM_B is | must still verify | **`6 verified, 0 errors`** — the ARM_B/ARM_C spelling asymmetry is **cosmetic**, not load-bearing |

✅ **So ARM_C is not vacuous in any of the three senses `.memory/04-verus.md`
names, and the arm reproduces in the shipped machinery.** That attack does not
land, and the next agent should not re-run it.

**Now the one that does land.** `.memory/04-verus.md`: *"the vacuity probe is not
'is the postcondition true?' but **'what is the CHEAPEST body that satisfies
it?'** Write that body and run it."*

```rust
#[cfg(ARM_C)]
fn arm_c() -> (r: u8)
    ensures r == 9u8,
{
    9u8            // no allocation, no pointer, no permission, no read
}
                              -> verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors
```

> ⚠⚠⚠ **ARM_C's postcondition is discharged by a CONSTANT FUNCTION, at the same
> `6 verified, 0 errors`.** So *"it does not merely fail to complain — it
> **proves** the stale read returns the recycled occupant's value"* is a reading
> of the **body**. The **specification** licenses nothing about recycling,
> pointers or permissions: it says the answer is `9`.

**And the R5 cannot even HOLD a stale permission.** The FIND saving the
permission rather than the address is not a verification failure — it does not
compile:

```
error[E0502]: cannot borrow `pt` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
```

⚠ **So linearity is not *blind* to the recycle. It makes the stale read
UNWRITABLE and forces the USE to present the CURRENT permission** — which is
exactly why the value comes back as `9`. In C the read is stale; in R5 the same
source line is, by construction, a fresh read of a live record whose occupant has
changed. **That is a functional bug, and it is not the same object as the C bug.**

**And the shipped-convention obligation rejects it.** ARM_D fails; its must-fire
control — the identical `ensures r == 7` on the program with the splice removed —
**verifies `6 verified, 0 errors`**, so ARM_D's failure is caused by the splice
and not by an unachievable postcondition. And §2e's `26/26` reproduces exactly
(`.temp/t137/logs/foldcensus.log`; a plain grep for `_fold(` gives **20**, because
six patterns name the fold `wrapping_sum`, `copy_sum`, `st_fold`, `key_fold`,
`op_fold`, `bn_fold` — the JSON parse gives **26 of 26**).

> ### ⚠⚠⚠ THE CORRECTED SENTENCE
>
> ✅ **What STANDS, and it is `TASK_136`'s real contribution: *what linearity
> states is "no use after DEALLOCATION"; it cannot state "no use after the
> OCCUPANT CHANGED".*** That scoping of `RECAP` 47 is right and should land.
>
> ⚠⚠ **What FALLS is the clause built on top of it: *"`p42`'s failure mode is
> available here IN AN R5 THAT LOOKS COMPLETELY HEALTHY"*, and *"the strongest
> vindication that [the attack-arm] rule has had"*.** `p42`'s failure mode is an
> R5 that **states its obligation**, verifies, and leaks. **No `p29` R5 that
> states this project's obligation verifies with the bug present** — ARM_D does
> not, and 26/26 fences force ARM_D's shape. What rejects the bug is the fold
> postcondition **every pattern already pins**, not an arm added because of the
> rule. **The rule was not vindicated here; it was not needed here.**
>
> ⚠⚠⚠ **AND THERE *IS* A REAL `p42`-SHAPED RISK FOR `p29`. IT IS A DIFFERENT
> ONE, AND IT IS THE SENTENCE THAT SHOULD REPLACE THE PUBLISHED ONE:** if
> `p29_fold` in `verus.rs` is **transliterated from the kernel** instead of

> That is item 5's hazard at the R5 level — `p23`'s — and it is live, because

## 4 — ⚠⚠⚠ ITEM 3: THE RECONCILIATION FALLS. Right numbers, wrong variable.

`TASK_136` §2d, landed in `RECAP` 49 and 51: *"`TASK_133`'s reading is not simply
wrong — it measured a DIFFERENT SPELLING. Its index arena RECYCLES SLOTS. Four
builds of one safe source: recycling takes the fuzz failures `17 → 36` and adds a
hand input. **So the variable is SLOT RECYCLING, not the language.**"*

⚠⚠ **`TASK_133`'s arena is `Vec<Node>`, not `Vec<Option<Node>>`, and its own
source says what it does:**

```rust
// .temp/t133/b_express/r29_safeidx.rs
// "free" is a free-list push.  Nothing is deallocated; the Vec owns the
// storage from beginning to end.
fn release(&mut self, i: u32) { self.free.push(i); }
```

**The record survives its own release.** `TASK_136`'s `safe.rs` writes
`tab[cur] = None` in **both** of its builds, destroying the record either way; its
`--cfg recycle` therefore varies **which slot a later insert takes**, not
**whether the freed record is still readable**. Those are different mechanisms,
and only one of them needs a subsequent INSERT to bite.

`.temp/t137/c/safe137.rs` is the engineer's own source with **one** new arm,
`--cfg keepdead`, which does what `TASK_133`'s `release` does.
`.temp/t137/logs/reconcile.log`:

```
       input |   C R1 (ASan) |   t136 default   t136 +recycle        KEEPDEAD  KEEPDEAD+recyc   KEEPDEAD+line
    v5  deg0 |    ASan-abort |             OK              OK  69224958378945  69224958378945              OK
    v15 deg0 |    ASan-abort |             OK              OK  69224958448385  69224958448385              OK
    v25 deg0 |    ASan-abort |             OK              OK  69224958517825  69224958517825              OK
   successor |    ASan-abort |             OK              OK  69224958448385  69224958448385              OK

fuzz, 700 windows; windows where C R1 ABORTS under ASan (the use-after-FREE class): 71

            build     wrong TOTAL     wrong ON THE INPUTS WHERE C ABORTS
     t136 default              17                                 0 / 71
    t136 +recycle              36                                19 / 71
         KEEPDEAD              88                                71 / 71
   KEEPDEAD+recyc              88                                71 / 71
    KEEPDEAD+line               0                                 0 / 71
      KD+rec+line               0                                 0 / 71
```

> ### ⚠⚠⚠ THREE THINGS AT ONCE
>
> 1. **Slot recycling explains `19` of the `71` and NONE of `TASK_133`'s
>    PUBLISHED DATA POINTS.** `TASK_136`'s own §2d table prints **`OK` on `v5`,
>    `v15` and `v25`** — the three leaf inputs `TASK_133` published as *silently

>
> ✅ **And the line still fixes it: `KEEPDEAD+line` is `0`.**

**This is `.memory/03-measurement.md` failure-class entry 12 exactly.** `17`,

property every headline turns on is on the **read path**, and three structurally
different read-path implementations agree on every input measured:

(`saved.key == skey and _in(root, saved)`); the engineer's **`H5`**, which
re-derives by key at read time (**1511** inputs, `k29.c` shape); and my **`T3`**,
an O(1) slot/key test (**614** inputs, pinned shape). Three different ways of
asking the question, zero disagreements. **`SPEC_EXACT` is corroborated, not
merely asserted** — which is what the disclosure needed and did not have.

⚠⚠ **But the fix was for one bug, not for the class.** `.temp/t136/p29c/model.py`'s
REMOVE is a **line-by-line transliteration** of `kernel.c`'s REMOVE — the same
variable names (`cur`, `par`, `goleft`, `guard`, `sp`, `s`, `sgoleft`), the same
`guard < CAP + 1` bound, the same *"move the cursor to the successor"* step, in
the same order. Its header claims independence *"in the sense the gate means
it: it has no slot table, no pointers and no `live[]`"* — true, and beside the
point. `safe.rs`'s REMOVE is a transliteration too.

> ⚠ **Concrete and actionable: if `patterns/p29-*/model.py` inherits this file,
> `check.py`'s model-sandbox rule is satisfied MECHANICALLY and defeated IN

## 6 — ITEM 4: THE CONVENTION CENSUS SURVIVES

The task file named the failure mode: *"a hardened cell that adds a conjunct
spelled across two lines, or as an early `return`, would be classified
`False`."* `.temp/t137/c/convention137.py` re-runs the same question with the
statement joined — candidates are single added lines **and every concatenation of
2..4 consecutive added lines**, matched against the same runs of removed lines:

```
patterns shipping c/kernel_hardened.c            : 25
STRICT  (t136's line-based classifier)           : 4  ['p17', 'p22', 'p23', 'p27']
JOINED  (allows a conjunct across up to 4 lines) : 4  ['p17', 'p22', 'p23', 'p27']
newly admitted by relaxing the line boundary     : []
```

✅ **Zero new admissions.** And I read all 21 non-conjunct hunks
(`.temp/t137/logs/convention137.log` dumps every one) rather than trusting the
bucketing. The buckets are right. Spot-checks: `SLB_P19_TBL = SLB_P19_NST × 256
= 8 × 256 = 2048`, so *"a 2048-iteration validation loop"* is exact; `p42` really
is `return 0;` → `goto cleanup;`; `p13` really is one unconditional store;
`p47` really is two declarations plus an or-accumulate loop.

⚠ **One narrowing, and it does not change the count.** The classifier tests a

## 9 — CLEAN NEGATIVES: named attacks that did NOT land. Do not re-run these.

1. **"`H2` is a fix that fits the measured inputs."** No. 14 hand inputs
   including 5 written to break it, 600 fresh windows, `0`. **And it is exact for
   a reason** (§1): the substitution raises a record's key monotonically, so the
   found key can never come back.
2. **"ARM_C is vacuous."** No, in all three of `.memory/04-verus.md`'s senses:
   `assert(false)` fails at the end **and** immediately after `rec_open` (so the
   `external_body` axioms are consistent), and `ensures r == 8` fails.
3. **"ARM_B and ARM_C are not the same machinery — ARM_B goes through
   `Map::tracked_borrow` and ARM_C does not."** Cosmetic: ARM_C rewritten
   through `p27`'s permission `Map` still gives `6 verified, 0 errors`.
4. **"ARM_D fails for some reason other than the splice."** No: the identical
   `ensures r == 7` on the program with the splice removed verifies `6/0`.
5. **"`convention.py` misses a conjunct spelled across lines."** It cannot see
   one, but there is none: relaxing the line boundary to 4 lines admits nothing.
6. **"§2e's `26/26` is inflated."** No — it reproduces exactly. (A plain grep for
   `_fold(` gives 20 and would look like a refutation; six patterns name the fold
   something else.)
7. **"The disclosed model/implementation defect contaminated another number."**
   Not one that is published — three structurally different read-path
   implementations agree (§5). The **class** is still live in the artefact,
   which is a different and smaller claim.
8. **"ASan is blind on this box."** Positive control fires in every probe
   (`rc=1 hits=2 heap-use-after-free`), and `H4` fires 82 times on the same
   corpus where `T3` fires zero.

## 10 — WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHAT I AM UNSURE OF

- **No cost axis was measured.** I publish no rung-to-rung difference. ⚠ **So I
  cannot say whether `T3` or `H2` is cheaper, and that may be the criterion that
  decides §7 item 1.** Note `T3` moves work to the READ op and `H2` to the DELETE
  op, so the answer will depend on the op mix `gen.py` produces — which is a
  reason to decide it before the inputs are pinned, not after.
- **`T3` was measured in ONE kernel shape** (the pinned slot table), one
  compiler, one optimisation level. I did not search other spellings of the
  read-path line beyond `T3`/`T4`, and I did not try to find a **one**-conjunct
  exact read-path line; I argue there is none (§2c) and I did not prove it.
- **I did not run Miri** on the safe rung. `TASK_136` disclosed that gap and it
  is unchanged; my `keepdead` arm is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and has no UB to
  find, but I did not confirm that with the tool.
- **I did not re-derive the engineer's numbers**, per the task file. Where mine
  overlap theirs (`H2` exact, `H1` misses, R1's harm split, the reproducibility
  invariant, the `25`/`4` census, `26/26`) they agree; where they do not overlap
  I did not check.
- **The `p42`-shaped risk I name in §3b is an ARGUMENT, not a measurement.** I
  did not build a transliterated `p29_fold` and show it verifies the bug. It
  follows immediately from ARM_C, but a build task should probably spend ten
  minutes proving it rather than trusting me.
- ⚠ **I am reporting `T3` as a refutation of a published sentence, not as a
  recommendation.** I have **not** shown `T3` is the better R1h; I have shown the
  choice was closed on a false premise and is therefore open.
